body: Tuesday, February 03 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: Bullish on growth, bearish on duration. The January ISM manufacturing PMI jumped to 52.6%, the fastest gains since 2022, and the S&P 500 flirted with a record high as chipmakers and small caps jumped. The catch: the January employment report will be delayed by the partial government shutdown, so the market is trading one survey and a hawkish Fed pick without its main labour gauge.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.57% and the 10Y at 4.29%, a 72 bps 10Y−2Y spread; over 20 observations both rose 10 bps on rounded figures, a move classed as bear steepening (both up, 10Y up more) that leaves the curve moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-02). Over five observations the 10Y rose 7 bps against 1 bp for the 2Y (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-02). The S&P 500 closed at 6,976.44, up 0.54%, with the VIX down 1.1 points to 16.34 and the DXY up 0.64% to 97.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

New / Most Important: Treasury yields ticked higher on the strong data as traders weighed the Warsh pick, whom they read as the more hawkish choice. Washington also agreed to cut tariffs on India to 18% after India agreed to end Russian oil purchases — a trade de-escalation that removes one inflation risk while the shutdown blinds the Fed's labour read. Stronger factories, a tougher chair and missing payrolls together argue for owning cyclicals while keeping duration light.

Playbook ✓: Own cyclicals over duration: industrials, small caps — IWM closed at 262.18, up 1.02% — and banks, and stay underweight TLT, which fell 0.67% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Add duration only if the 10Y falls back below 4.19%, its level 20 observations earlier (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-02); cut cyclicals if the delayed payrolls fail to confirm the ISM jump.

Macro Stance: Bullish. Banks drove European stocks to a record high as markets recovered from a rocky start: the STOXX 600 closed at 617.31, up 1.03%, and the FTSE 100 at 10,341.60, up 1.16% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Germany's manufacturing sector is showing signs of recovery, the PMI indicates.

Activity & Inflation: The cycle is turning at the factory gate, but margins are not: euro-zone firms see deteriorating profits, the ECB's access-to-finance survey shows. Volume up and pricing power down is the mix that keeps the ECB on hold rather than hiking, and it argues for owning lenders over price-takers. Germany's PMI turn matters most because it has been the region's laggard.

New / Most Important: Reuters frames the ECB meeting around five questions under the banner 'no escaping the euro or the Fed'. EUR/USD fell 0.97% to 1.1849 as the dollar rebounded and the DAX rose 1.05% to 24,797.52 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) — a softer euro eases the squeeze on exporters.

Playbook ✓: Stay long euro-area banks and domestic cyclicals — the record was bank-led — and add selectively to exporters while EUR/USD holds below 1.1849 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Trim banks if the ECB signals enough concern about corporate margins to hint at a cut, which would flatten curves and hit net interest income.

Macro Stance: Bearish. Factory data split — the official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3 while a private gauge showed expansion for export-oriented firms — but property, land revenue and markets all deteriorated. Policy is easing at the margin, not by enough to offset a housing relapse that drags on household confidence and local budgets.

PMIs & Activity: The official PMI at 49.3 reflects soft domestic orders, while the private gauge for export-oriented firms expanded. The split says exporters are coping and the domestic economy is not; confirmation of a broader turn needs the official gauge back above 50 after the Lunar New Year distortions wash out.

Credit Impulse: No January credit print is in the feed yet. Price is moving instead of volume: the PBOC's key bank loan rate fell to a record low, which helps willing borrowers but does not create demand from households that are deleveraging. A rebound in January new loans and social financing is what would confirm an impulse.

Property: The January relief rally is fading: SCMP reports a 'bleak start' to 2026 as property sales declines accelerate, and local governments logged a double-digit drop in land-sale income for a fourth straight year in 2025. Lower land revenue squeezes local budgets exactly where infrastructure support would have to come from.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Fiscal support stays narrow: with land income shrinking, Beijing is leaning on monetary plumbing rather than budget stimulus. Externally, Xi's 'strong currency' mission to make the yuan a global reserve rules out a devaluation to rescue exporters; USD/CNY held at 6.9510, down 0.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Markets & Flows: Hong Kong stocks dropped by the most since November, led by mining and telecoms: the Hang Seng closed at 26,775.57, down 2.23%, and the Shanghai Composite at 4,015.75, down 2.48% and now 0.19% lower over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). ASHR is down 0.72%, KWEB 1.57% and FXI 1.63% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) — January's gains are gone.

New / Most Important: The metals crash transmitted straight into Hong Kong, where mining led the drop, and property sales are weakening again. Together they suggest the late-January rally on eased developer rules was a positioning trade that has run its course, while the record-low loan rate shows Beijing still prefers incremental easing to a big stimulus.

Playbook ✓: Underweight China beta (FXI, ASHR) and avoid developers; keep only exporter and AI-hardware exposure that the private PMI supports. Turn constructive if the official PMI returns above 50 and January credit data rebound; cut further if the Hang Seng loses 26,347.24, its level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). ⚠ Divergence: the private factory gauge for exporters is expanding and the PBOC loan rate is at a record low — if exporters keep hiring, the bearish property story may overstate the hit to listed earnings.

Macro Stance: Bullish. A survey shows the LDP-JIP coalition on track for a two-thirds majority, and the BOJ's January summary showed members debating the risk of falling behind the curve on inflation. A supermajority plus a hawkish-leaning central bank is a reflation mix for domestic earnings and for banks.

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY rose 1.33% to 155.20 after Takaichi's comment cooled intervention speculation, while the Nikkei 225 fell 1.25% to 52,655.18 but is still up 4.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Reuters notes Takaichi must face bond investors before she wins over voters, so fiscal promises are being priced in the JGB curve.

Playbook ✓: Own exporters again on a weaker yen and keep domestic banks for the BOJ angle, while hedging long-end JGB exposure into the vote. Cut if USD/JPY reverses its 1.33% one-day rise (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) on renewed intervention talk, or if bond investors force a fiscal retreat.

Macro Stance: Bearish for domestic equities. A rate hike is expected at Tuesday's RBA meeting, a U-turn that breaks from the global easing trend, and market experts are pricing higher odds of an increase. Tightening into a strong currency raises the hurdle for the whole market.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD fell 1.43% to 0.6946 as the dollar rebounded but is still up 3.93% over 20 sessions, while the ASX 200 fell 1.02% to 8,778.60 and is up only 0.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). The currency has done part of the RBA's tightening, and equities have stopped rewarding good news.

Playbook ✓: Underweight rate-sensitive ASX sectors into the decision and prefer bank margins over housing-linked names. A hike with a hawkish statement should lift AUD again; a hold would push it toward 0.6684, its level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), and favour ASX rate-sensitives on relief.

Monetary & Activity: Poland's manufacturing PMI edged up in January, with industry optimism at its highest in years, Rzeczpospolita reports. MPC member Kotecki has said a cut could come as early as February — easing into an improving factory cycle, the best mix for domestic equities.

FX & Markets: The zloty weakened with the dollar rebound: USD/PLN rose 1.17% to 3.5548 and EUR/PLN closed at 4.2117; EPOL added 0.19%, PKO BP 0.99% and Pekao 2.12%, while KGHM fell 5.99% and is down 12.25% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Money.pl reports KGHM lost 15% at the open as the metals selloff hit the Warsaw floor.

Companies: Remigiusz Paszkiewicz now runs KGHM, so the stock trades on copper and silver rather than on the leadership change. Allegro is under fire, with Erli filing a lawsuit after InPost; ALE rose 1.69% in the prior session but is down 4.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Security & New Development: Poland picked a Kongsberg-PGZ consortium to build its anti-drone 'wall', channelling defence spending to a domestic partner. With a February cut possible, fiscal and monetary policy both lean pro-growth.

Playbook ✓: Own PKO BP and Pekao for growth and dividends and keep zloty exposure while EUR/PLN holds near 4.21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02); re-enter KGHM only after copper, down 1.62% to 5.80, stabilises. ⚠ Divergence: the PMI shows the best industry optimism in years, yet the WIG20TR ETF rose only 0.12% and KGHM keeps falling (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) — Warsaw is trading global metals, not Polish growth.

Narrative: Tech is a two-speed sector: XLK rose 0.96% as AAPL jumped 4.06%, while MSFT fell 1.61% and ORCL 2.75% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Wall Street now openly talks about haves and have-nots in tech after earnings.

Reported: Palantir beat fourth-quarter estimates on the strength of AI and defense demand, the clearest counterexample to the 'software is dead' trade. Oracle's $25 billion bond sale helped ease fears of an AI debt wave, yet ORCL is down 18.22% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Monetisers with a lowered bar: PLTR's beat arrived with the stock down 11.97% over 20 sessions, and AAPL's 4.06% jump shows investors paying for record hardware demand despite memory costs (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Estimate revisions, not multiple expansion, can carry both.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The split is not hardware versus software but AI monetisation versus AI cost: Palantir is growing revenue on AI demand while Oracle has to borrow to build. Own the monetisers and fund them from the financed-capex names.

Narrative: Communication services hinges on the week's platform prints: Alphabet and Amazon report alongside the delayed jobs data and more Warsh fallout. GOOGL rose 1.68% to 343.69 and is up 9.06% over 20 sessions, while XLC slipped 0.34% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Reported: Disney shares fell despite streaming growth as the CEO decision nears, losing 7.4% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Legacy media is being valued on succession risk, not on the quarter.

EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet: search, YouTube and cloud all monetise AI directly, and the bar is a revenue-led beat rather than a capex headline. META slipped 1.41% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), so platform expectations are not stretched going in.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Disney's drop despite growth shows old-media multiples are capped by governance, not demand. XLC is a bet on AI platforms; underweight legacy media through management transitions.

Narrative: Financials led the rebound: XLF rose 1.1%, BAC 1.56% and GS 1.17% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), mirroring the bank-led record in Europe. A stronger ISM and a bear-steepening curve support loan growth and margins.

Reported: The micro news was a warning rather than a trend: Chicago's Metropolitan Capital Bank became the first US bank failure of 2026. JPM rose 0.74% to 308.14 but is still down 5.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Capital-markets franchises: record-pace bond issuance (see the flows section) and recovering equity markets feed fees at GS and the large banks, whose shares lag the S&P 500's 1.72% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).
⚡ Breaking Convention: The tail sits in private credit: UBS's worst case for AI disruption has private-credit defaults hitting 13%. Own the money-centre banks, avoid BDCs with software-heavy books.

Narrative: The Iran premium is unwinding: oil settled down more than 4% on US-Iran de-escalation, with Brent down 6.21% to 66.30, WTI down 4.71% to 62.14, XLE down 1.96% and XOM down 2.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Reported: Exxon beat as Permian and Guyana fields took output to a 40-year high — the majors' story is volume. XOM is still up 12.84% and CVX 11.63% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), gains built partly on a supply-shock premium now being negotiated away.

EPS Upside Watch: Gas is the downside surprise: US natural-gas prices plummeted on warmer forecasts, with Henry Hub down 25.65% to 3.24 in one session and 52.4% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Gas-weighted producers' first-quarter estimates are too high; refiners with cheaper feedstock are the relative winners.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Talks, not strikes: US-Iran nuclear talks are expected Friday. If they hold, Brent's remaining 9.14% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) is the next leg to unwind — the 'geopolitical floor' under oil is weaker than consensus assumes.

Narrative: Industrials are the macro winner: the January ISM rose to 52.6% and industrials were among the leaders of Monday's rally. CAT jumped 5.1% to 690.91 and XLI rose 1.26% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Reported: Results season for the big industrials is largely behind us; the read-through now comes from the data, with US factory activity posting its fastest gains since 2022. CAT is up 15.46% over 20 sessions and GE rose 0.63% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Short-cycle names — machinery, distributors, transports — gain most from an ISM back above 50, and the Russell 2000 rose 1.02% to 2,640.28 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) as investors began to price it. Defence primes add a second leg on European demand.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Breadth is the surprise: a manufacturing rebound turns the AI-capex-only industrial trade into a cyclical one, which favours laggards such as BA, down 6.2% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Narrative: Discretionary is still K-shaped: the economy has turned restaurant winners and losers upside down, Business Insider reports. XLY rose 0.66% while TSLA fell 2.0% and HD rose 0.94% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Reported: Tyson topped estimates on strong chicken sales and its stock rose, while Disney's streaming growth did not save its shares. Spending is holding up; share reactions diverge on company-specific issues.

EPS Upside Watch: Amazon headlines the busiest week of the reporting period with Alphabet; AMZN rose 1.53% to 242.96 and is up 7.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). AWS growth and retail margins are the swing factors for a beat.
⚡ Breaking Convention: The K-shape means averages mislead: value chains and premium brands both win while the middle loses. Own the extremes and avoid mid-priced casual dining and mall retail.

Narrative: Staples keep winning the rotation: XLP rose 1.19% and is up 8.77% over 20 sessions, with WMT up 4.13% to 124.06 and COST 2.99% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Defensive demand survived even a strong-data day.

Reported: Tyson topped earnings estimates on strong chicken sales and the stock rose — protein demand is resilient in a K-shaped consumer economy. XLV and XLP both rose in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), a sign defensives are not being sold to fund cyclicals.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart and Costco are the price-makers: WMT is up 10.02% and COST 13.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), and both sit at the value end of the K-shaped consumer.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples rallying on an ISM-surprise day is unusual — the bid looks like rotation money that can leave if cyclicals keep working. Trim XLP into strength if payrolls confirm the factory rebound.

Narrative: Healthcare is still the policy sector: XLV is up only 0.12% over 20 sessions while UNH is down 15.1% and LLY 3.35% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). PBMs were hit by a Trump transparency rule, adding to the managed-care squeeze.

Reported: Revvity forecast 2026 profit and revenue above estimates after a blowout fourth quarter, so tools demand is not uniformly weak. UNH slipped 0.47% to 285.59 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Obesity volume remains the sector's one clear estimate upside, and LLY rose 0.67% to 1,044.13 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Life-science tools are the second candidate after Revvity's guide.
⚡ Breaking Convention: PBM reform hurts the middlemen but can help drugmakers' net pricing — winners and losers sit inside the same sector. Short managed care and PBMs against long branded pharma.

Narrative: Materials split between a precious-metals unwind and a strategic-minerals bid: gold and silver fell further as a CME margin hike stoked selling, while Trump launched a $12 billion minerals stockpile to counter China. XLB rose 0.77% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Reported: The tape, not results, set the tone: copper extended its slump as traders eyed volatility across metals, with the front month down 1.62% to 5.80, while FCX rose 0.88% and NEM 0.45% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).
EPS Upside Watch: Critical-minerals producers: a $12 billion stockpile creates a price-insensitive buyer for strategic minerals, an estimate tailwind that has not yet reached company guidance.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Consensus treats metals as one trade; the stockpile splits them into state-backed demand for strategic minerals versus margin-driven liquidation in gold and silver. Own the strategic producers, not the bullion proxies.
Narrative: REITs fell 1.13% as the 10Y rose to 4.29% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-02). A hotter ISM and a hawkish Fed pick push rate relief further out.

Reported: The credit signal is household stress: more homeowners are falling behind on their mortgages as affordability bites. That is a risk for residential and mortgage REITs more than for data-centre landlords.

EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre and industrial landlords tied to the manufacturing upturn and the AI build-out keep pricing power, but XLRE's 1.44% 20-session gain lags the S&P 500's 1.72% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), so selection matters more than beta.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Rising mortgage stress would eventually pull long yields down — the REIT bear case carries its own hedge. Pair an underweight in mortgage REITs with a small long in long-duration Treasuries.

Narrative: Utilities lost the defensive bid: XLU fell 1.46% and is down 1.3% over 20 sessions, while CEG fell 3.49% and VST 2.58% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Higher yields and collapsing gas prices both hurt.

Reported: The EIA says US wholesale day-ahead electricity prices rose in 2025 with higher natural-gas prices — the tailwind merchant generators rode. With Henry Hub down 25.65% in a session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), that tailwind is reversing.

EPS Upside Watch: Regulated names with rate-base growth hold up best: NEE is still up 6.67% over 20 sessions despite a 1.79% drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Contracted data-centre load matters more than spot power prices.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Cheap gas is bullish for data-centre economics and for industrial power users, but bearish for the stocks that sold the AI-power story: CEG is down 26.04% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). The AI-power trade is migrating from generators to equipment makers.

Narrative: European autos bounced with the market — the SXAP tracker rose 0.72% — but remain down 4.29% over 20 sessions, with Renault down 10.48% and Stellantis 13.31% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Chinese competition and EV price wars have not gone away.

Reported: European automakers are rethinking software independence, a strategic retreat after years of in-house platform spending. BMW rose 0.66% and Mercedes 1.09% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).
EPS Upside Watch: A firmer dollar helps: EUR/USD fell 0.97% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), a translation tailwind for German premium brands' US sales if it persists.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Partnering on software could cut capex faster than the market expects — the bear case assumes Europe keeps spending to compete alone. VOW3, down only 0.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02), is the relative winner if costs fall.

Narrative: Semis rebounded: SOXX rose 1.85%, MU 5.52%, INTC 5.04% and TSM 3.27% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). TrendForce sees chip prices surging 90-95% in the first quarter from the previous quarter — the memory cycle is now about price, not just volume.

Reported: NXP forecast an upbeat quarter, signalling an industrial market bottom, and Sandisk rocketed another 16%. Nvidia shares fell after a report that its OpenAI investment stalled, ending 2.89% lower (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

EPS Upside Watch: Memory and storage: a 90-95% first-quarter chip price jump flows almost straight to margins, and MU is up 38.8% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02) as estimates chase. Analog names gain from the industrial bottom NXP flagged.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The GPU leader is the laggard: NVDA is down 1.72% over 20 sessions while MU is up 38.8% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Scarcity, not share, drives returns — own memory and equipment over the accelerator crowd, and treat any memory-price rollover as the signal to rotate back.

Rewarded: Pricing power and proven demand: Sandisk rocketed another 16%, Tyson rose after beating on chicken sales, and AAPL jumped 4.06% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Palantir, beating on AI and defense demand, and NXP, with an upbeat guide, reported after the close and are the next tests of whether beats get paid.

Punished: Disney fell despite streaming growth — governance trumped the quarter — and the AI spenders kept bleeding: MSFT is down 10.48% and ORCL 18.22% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Even a $25 billion bond sale that eased AI-debt fears did not lift Oracle's stock.

Pattern: Wall Street sees a divide between tech haves and have-nots after earnings: revenue that proves AI demand is rewarded, capex that must be financed is not. A beat alone is not enough; the reaction follows whether the print changes the funding or growth story. Governance can override both, as Disney's succession overhang showed in the same session.

Attention into EPS: Alphabet and Amazon report in a week that also carries more Warsh fallout, Yahoo Finance previews AMD's quarter, and the jobs report will be delayed — so earnings, not payrolls, set the macro tone. Alphabet must show cloud acceleration; AMD must address accelerator timing.

Playbook: Buy monetisers on post-earnings dips (PLTR, memory) and fade financed-capex stories until free cash flow stabilises. Stop the long-monetiser, short-spender pair if MSFT reclaims 472.94, its close 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Attention Gap: The January ISM jumped to 52.6%, the fastest gains since 2022, yet hedge funds have been trimming North America exposure amid trade tensions, dollar pain and megacap weakness. The money is leaving US megacaps just as the data turn in favour of domestic cyclicals those funds are not chasing.

Exposure & Risk: Express via IWM (262.18, up 5.39% over 20 sessions) and XLI (167.53) rather than megacaps (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Risk: one survey is not a cycle, payrolls are delayed, and a hawkish Fed would hit small caps' floating-rate debt first.

Attention Gap: A two-thirds majority for the LDP-JIP coalition plus a BOJ worried about being behind the curve is a rate-and-spending mix. Attention is on the yen; the cleaner beneficiary is bank net interest income.

Exposure & Risk: Express via MUFG, SMFG and Mizuho ADRs while hedging the yen, given USD/JPY's 1.33% one-day rise to 155.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Risk: a JGB selloff if fiscal promises spook bond investors, which would hit bank bond books before it lifts margins.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 78,688.77, up 2.23% on the day but down 11.77% over five sessions and 17.45% over 20; ether closed at 2,344.36, down 22.03% over five, and solana at 104.47, down 28.13% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). In US trading IBIT fell 6.89% to 44.22, MSTR 6.73% and COIN 3.53% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). Bitcoin briefly tumbled below $75K, though some investors see a buying opportunity.

New / Most Important: Strategy slid after bitcoin briefly dipped below the firm's key breakeven level, and crypto-exchange stocks have lost more than 55% on a retail exodus. Policy is stuck too: the stablecoin-yield deadlock persists in White House talks between banks and crypto firms. The exchange drawdown is a volume story — retail activity, not just prices, is shrinking, which removes the marginal buyer that powered last year's rallies.

Playbook: Stay underweight crypto equities; the weakest link is leverage at treasury companies trading near their bitcoin cost. Use IBIT for any re-entry and only after bitcoin holds above $75K on daily closes; a stablecoin compromise is the policy catalyst that would change the call.

Rates & Dollar: The dollar advanced on safe-haven flows and strong US data: the DXY rose 0.64% to 97.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02). The 10Y closed at 4.29% and the 30Y at 4.90%, with the 10Y up 7 bps over five observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-02), while TLT fell 0.67% to 86.55 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).

Credit Check: Supply is enormous but clearing: global bond sales reached $1 trillion at their fastest pace ever, and Oracle's $25 billion deal eased fears of an AI debt wave. HYG slipped 0.43% and LQD 0.46% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02); the stress is in private credit, where UBS's worst case puts AI-related defaults at 13%.

Portfolio Implication: Hold equities over bonds while issuance clears and the ISM improves; keep duration short and IG in the front end, where carry is decent and supply pressure is lighter. A failed or heavily discounted AI mega-deal would be the signal to cut credit beta; until then the cheapest hedge is the long-dollar sleeve that rallied on the strong data.

What Is Priced: Market experts are pricing higher odds of a cash-rate increase at Tuesday's meeting, a U-turn against the global easing trend. AUD/USD is still up 3.93% over 20 sessions at 0.6946 despite a 1.43% drop in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-02).
